oil.summary: Crude remains under severe pressure with WTI at $75.34 (-0.93% on the day, -30.66% over the month) and Brent barely holding $79 after the Strait of Hormuz reopening removed the geopolitical risk premium that had supported prices. Despite a bullish EIA print — US crude stocks drew 8.3 million barrels in the week ending June 12 — the macro supply narrative is overwhelmingly bearish. Analysts warn that global inventory builds in the region will absorb Iranian barrels swiftly, undermining any Iran-peace optimism. Meanwhile, G7 leaders agreed to escalate sanctions on Russian crude, with Trump vowing reimposition 'soon,' though the market appears to be pricing this as a lagging offset rather than an immediate bullish catalyst. TotalEnergies flagged that a key Saudi refinery damaged during the conflict will not fully recover until early 2027, adding a modest downstream supply-quality caveat. Falling Murban and Dubai benchmarks have opened arbitrage windows to the US and Europe.
drivers: Hormuz reopening and anticipated Iranian supply return dominating sentiment, overwhelming a large 8.3 mb crude draw reported by EIA
G7 agreement on escalated Russian crude sanctions and Trump's reimposition signals add geopolitical optionality but not yet price support
TotalEnergies warns damaged Saudi refinery offline until 2027, creating product-quality and refinery-throughput uncertainty in the medium term

gas.summary: Natural gas markets are diverging sharply across hubs. Henry Hub slipped 2.32% on the day to $3.164/MMBtu but remains up 4.63% on the month, suggesting US domestic fundamentals are relatively firmer. TTF, by contrast, fell 0.74% today and is down 17.06% on the week and the month, consistent with the post-Hormuz easing of European supply anxiety. The G7's agreement to escalate sanctions on Russian gas exports introduces a potential upside risk for TTF that the market has not yet priced fully. On the supply side, ExxonMobil signing a preliminary LNG supply deal for South Africa's first import terminal underscores the continued build-out of Atlantic Basin LNG demand. Headline flow for this sector is limited today; the dominant driver remains the geopolitical repricing post-Iran ceasefire.
drivers: TTF under heavy weekly and monthly selling pressure as Hormuz reopening eases European supply stress
G7 sanctions escalation on Russian gas exports represents an unpriced upside risk for TTF that traders are watching
ExxonMobil LNG supply deal for South Africa's first import terminal signals ongoing incremental demand growth in emerging markets

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs held near flat today at $75.44 (-0.17%) but are up 3.05% on the week and 5.61% on the month, a notable divergence from the collapsing energy commodity complex — likely reflecting structural decarbonization demand rather than near-term fuel-switching dynamics. TTF's 17% weekly drop reduces gas-to-coal switching pressure, a mild near-term headwind for EUA demand. At the G7, UK PM Starmer pledged a £210 million nuclear energy package for Ukraine alongside fresh Russia sanctions. The IEA reported clean energy investment hit $2.2 trillion globally, nearly double fossil fuel spending — a structural tailwind for the power transition. AI-driven geothermal development is emerging as a niche but credible new demand theme. Poland approved a one-off windfall tax on fuel companies that profited during the Iran war, signalling broader European policy responses to the recent energy price shock.
drivers: EU EUAs outperforming broader energy complex with +5.61% monthly gain, underpinned by structural decarbonization demand despite weak gas prices
IEA data showing clean energy investment at $2.2 trillion — nearly double fossil fuels — reinforces long-run power transition momentum
G7 nuclear support for Ukraine and Poland's fuel windfall tax illustrate the widening policy response to the recent conflict-driven energy shock
